lines: Provides construction and engineering works (building and infrastructure), construction-related services and solutions, construction products (building materials, lighting, hardware, tools, machinery rental), and property development.
Serves property developers, contractors, government agencies, and retail customers across Malaysia.

Generates revenue from construction contracts, value-engineering fees under its BEST Collaboration Framework, product sales and rentals, and property sales; key strength is integrated model with G7 contractor status and RM1.52 billion orderbook.

matchedHeadings: financial information 11.1.3 consolidated statements of cash flows

data.trend: Revenue grew rapidly from FYE 2021 to FYE 2023 (over 5x), then stabilised in FYE 2024. Profit after tax rose strongly across the period, with net margin peaking in FYE 2022 before moderating and recovering in FYE 2024.
highlights: Revenue increased ~5.4x from RM67.4m to RM361.4m over four years
Profit after tax grew ~9.4x from RM7.9m to RM74.3m
Gross profit margin improved from 25.6% to 35.5%
Property development segment launched in FYE 2023, contributing 20% of revenue by FYE 2024

matchedHeadings: risk factors you should evaluate and carefully consider the following risks along with other information in this prospectus before investing in our company.

data.summary: Risk factors grouped by severity, ranking from most to least severe for investor impact.

themes.summary: Major customers contribute disproportionately to revenue (up to 95.91% in FYE 2023), making the company vulnerable to loss of key clients and significant financial impact.
Business performance heavily relies on continuous project acquisition; inability to secure new projects leads to declining orderbook and adverse financial consequences.
Unfavorable price fluctuations in construction materials, subcontractor costs, and labor can significantly increase project expenses and reduce profitability.
Delays in receivable collection and retention sum non-payment threaten cash flow and operational continuity, potentially impacting project execution.
Ongoing legal proceedings and CIDB certification dependencies could disrupt operations, halt projects, or impose significant financial burdens.
Competitive pressures, property market conditions, and economic downturns pose external threats to business performance and revenue stability.
Potential inadequacies in insurance coverage for certain risks like wars, terrorism, and natural disasters could result in large uncovered losses.

data.headline: Investors should monitor customer concentration, orderbook dependency, lock‑up restrictions, and related‑party transaction risks.

items.point: Customer concentration risk may cause sharp revenue drops if major clients reduce or terminate contracts.
items.why: High reliance on up to 95.91% of revenue from a few customers creates vulnerability.

items.point: Orderbook dependency means performance hinges on securing new construction projects; failure can shrink the RM1.52 billion orderbook.
items.why: Continuous project acquisition is critical for revenue and profit stability.

items.point: Lock‑up restrictions lock 602.5 million shares (71.87% of enlarged issued shares) for at least six months, limiting tradable supply.
items.why: Reduced liquidity can affect share price and exit flexibility for investors.

items.point: Related‑party transactions include sales, rentals, and loans with terms potentially more favorable than market rates, raising conflict‑of‑interest concerns.
items.why: These arrangements may impact fairness and future pricing.

relatedParty.summary: The prospectus discloses multiple material related-party transactions involving entities such as LSH Lighting, Knight Auto, LSHCC, LSH Holdings, and individuals including Lim Pak Lian and Lor Siew Hung. These transactions include sales of building materials, rentals of construction machinery and equipment, subcontracting works, loans with interest payments, and tenancy agreements. While most transactions are stated to be on arm's length terms, certain tenancy arrangements and loan interest rates are noted as being more favorable to the Group compared to market conditions. Some transactions were approved by non-interested shareholders at an EGM held on 28 March 2023.
